newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland march report speculation - Orange official.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland march report speculation - Orange official.

text.p: The BBC said on Thursday that the Orange Order had called off a planned parade through the Lower Ormeau Road in Northern Ireland's capital Belfast on Saturday to avoid violence.
But the Deputy Grand Master of the Protestant organisation, Jeffrey Donaldson, told another television network that no decision had yet been reached.
Donaldson, appearing on Ulster Television while the Orange Order was holding a Belfast news conference, said the membership was still deciding what to do.

"We are still waiting for members to come to a decision," said Donaldson, who is also a member of the British parliament for the province's main pro-British political group, the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).
Donaldson's mobile phone rang several times during an interview on the programme and he went off camera to take the calls but repeated that no decision had yet been made.
"It's purely a matter of speculation at this stage," he said.
The BBC quoted an Orange Order statement as saying that it had taken a "serious decision" not to parade down the Lower Ormeau Road, where it faces opposition from Catholic residents.
A packed news conference at an Orange Order lodge at one end of the Lower Ormeau Road awaited confirmation of the report.
The BBC said it had learned of the decision and had a document confirming that such a move had been made.
Earlier on Thursday Orange leaders held talks with police chiefs and a veteran Orange offical, James Molyneaux, a former head of the UUP.
Catholic residents had called on thousands of its supporters to descend on the area on Saturday to block the march, which is staged on the "Glorious 12th", the most hallowed date in its calendar.
It marks a 1690 victory by a Protestant king over an invading Catholic monarch which ensured a Protestant sat on the British throne.
Last Sunday Northern Ireland erupted into the worst violence for years after an Orange Order parade down the Catholic Garvaghy Road area of Portadown.
The Order, which is founded on its Protestant faith and British loyalty, has been under intense political pressure to call off Saturday's Belfast parade to avoid further violence.
